studies.title: Combinatorial therapy of LL-37 and ADSCs accelerates diabetic wound repair by orchestrating NRROS-mediated crosstalk between TGF-β/SMAD and hippo/TEAD1 axes.
studies.abstract: Diabetic wounds pose a significant therapeutic challenge. While the antimicrobial peptide LL-37 and adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) individually show potential for wound repair, the efficacy and mechanism of their combined treatment remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effect of LL-37 combined with ADSCs on diabetic wound healing. Clinical samples from diabetic and non-diabetic patients were analyzed, combined with bioinformatics analysis of public datasets (GSE144441 and GSE182906) to identify key genes. A diabetic mouse wound model was established to validate the healing effects of individual and combined LL-37 and ADSCs treatments. In vitro assays, co-culture models were employed to explore the mechanisms involving ADSCs and fibroblasts. Analysis of human diabetic wounds revealed impaired healing associated with deficiency in cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide (CAMP), the precursor of LL-37. In diabetic mice, the combination of LL-37 and ADSCs promoted wound healing more effectively than either treatment alone. LL-37 enhanced ADSC viability in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, LL-37 treatment significantly upregulated the expression of negative regulator of reactive oxygen species (NRROS) in ADSCs. Exosomes derived from these LL-37-primed ADSCs were taken up by fibroblasts, leading to increased NRROS expression in the recipient fibroblasts. Upregulated NRROS subsequently activated both the TGF-β/SMAD and Hippo/TEAD1 signaling pathways. Further experiments confirmed crosstalk between these two pathways, which collectively enhanced fibroblast proliferation and migration. In conclusion, the combination of LL-37 and ADSCs promotes diabetic wound healing by enhancing fibroblast activity. This effect is mediated through exosomal transfer of NRROS from ADSCs to fibroblasts, leading to the activation of the interconnected TGF-β/SMAD and Hippo/TEAD1 signaling pathways.

studies.title: The antibacterial effect of human adipose-derived stem cells on LL-37-resistant bacteria.
studies.abstract: Human adipose-derived stem cells (hADSCs) exhibit antibacterial properties, but their effectiveness against bacteria resistant to LL-37- a natural human antimicrobial peptide important in the immune defense- is not fully understood. Some bacteria have evolved mechanisms to evade the antimicrobial effects of LL-37. We aimed to investigate the antibacterial efficacy of hADSCs against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), focusing on the antimicrobial peptide LL-37. hADSCs were isolated from human adipose tissue, identified by flow cytometry and differentiation assays, and divided into three groups: unstimulated, stimulated with interferon-gamma (IFN-γ; 100 ng/mL) or Escherichia coli (300 CFU). LL-37 gene expression was measured by qPCR after 6 hours in the E. coli stimulated group. LL-37 peptide levels were quantified by ELISA in conditioned media from unstimulated, IFN-γ stimulated cells, both before and after incubation with pathogens (300 CFU). Antibacterial activity was assessed by colony counting incubation following incubation of conditioned media with bacteria. Conditioned media from both unstimulated and stimulated hADSCs significantly inhibited growth of all three pathogens (P < 0.05), with highest efficacy against P. aeruginosa (86.4% inhibition), followed by MRSA (74%) and P. mirabilis (63%). LL-37 gene expression increased after bacterial stimulation, and also LL-37 concentrations increased in conditioned media but significantly decreased after bacterial exposure (P < 0.05). Despite this reduction, antibacterial activity persisted. hADSC-conditioned media exert potent antibacterial effects against LL-37-resistant pathogens, even when LL-37 levels are reduced after bacterial exposure. These findings support the therapeutic potential of hADSC secretomes, particularly for infections caused by bacteria capable of reducing LL-37 levels.

studies.title: LL-37 improves sepsis-induced acute lung injury by suppressing pyroptosis in alveolar epithelial cells.
studies.abstract: LL-37 (also known as murine CRAMP) is a human antimicrobial peptide that plays a crucial role in innate immune defence against sepsis through various mechanisms. However, its involvement in sepsis-induced lung injury remains unclear. This work investigates the impact of LL-37 on pyroptosis generated by LPS in alveolar epithelial cells. The research utilizes both in vivo and in vitro sepsis-associated acute lung injury (ALI) models to understand the underlying molecular pathways. In vivo, an acute lung injury model induced by sepsis was established by intratracheal administration of LPS in C57BL/6J mice, which were subsequently treated with low-dose CRAMP (recombinant murine cathelicidin, 2.5 mg.kg The expression of NLRP3, caspase1 p20, NT-GSDMD, IL 18 and IL1β in the lung tissue of mice with septic lung injury was increased, which indicated activation of the canonical pyroptosis pathway and coincided with an increase in CRAMP expression. Treatment with recombinant CRAMP improved pyroptosis in mice with lung injury. In vitro, treatment with LPS and ATP upregulated these classic pyroptosis molecules, LL-37 knockdown exacerbated pyroptosis, and recombinant human LL-37 treatment alleviated pyroptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. These findings indicate that LL-37 protects against septic lung injury by modulating the expression of classic pyroptotic pathway components, including NLRP3, caspase1, and GSDMD and downstream inflammatory factors in alveolar epithelial cells.

studies.title: Cathelicidin LL-37 promotes wound healing in diabetic mice by regulating TFEB-dependent autophagy.
studies.abstract: Diabetic patients often experience impaired wound healing. Human cathelicidin LL-37 possesses various biological functions, such as anti-microbial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-wound healing activities. Autophagy has important effects on skin wound healing. However, little is known about whether LL-37 accelerates diabetic wound healing by regulating autophagy. In the study, we aimed to investigate the role of autophagy in LL-37-induced wound healing and uncover the underlying mechanisms involved. A full-thickness wound closure model was established in diabetic mice to evaluate the effects of LL-37 and an autophagy inhibitor (3-MA) on wound healing. The roles of LL-37 and 3-MA in regulating keratinocyte migration were assessed using transwell migration and wound healing assays. The activation of transcription factor EB (TFEB) was measured using western blotting and immunofluorescence (IF) assays of its nuclear translocation. The results showed that LL-37 treatment improved wound healing in diabetic mice, whereas these effects were reversed by 3-MA. In vitro, 3-MA decreased the effects of LL-37 on promoting HaCat keratinocyte migration in the presence of high glucose (HG). Mechanistically, LL-37 promoted TFEB activation and resulted in subsequent activation of autophagy, as evidenced by increased nuclear translocation of TFEB and increased expression of ATG5, ATG7, and beclin 1 (BECN1), whereas these changes were blocked by TFEB knockdown. As expected, TFEB knockdown damaged the effects of LL-37 on promoting keratinocyte migration. Collectively, these results suggest that LL-37 accelerates wound healing in diabetic mice by activating TFEB-dependent autophagy, providing new insights into the mechanism by which LL-37 promotes diabetic wound healing.

studies.title: Antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin LL-37 preserves intestinal barrier and organ function in rats with heat stroke.
studies.abstract: Global warming increases the incidence of heat stroke (HS) and HS causes the reduction of visceral blood flow during hyperthermia, leading to intestinal barrier disruption, microbial translocation, systemic inflammation and multiple organ failure. Cathelicidin LL-37 exhibits antimicrobial activities, helps innate immunity within the gut to maintain intestinal homeostasis, and augments intestinal wound healing and barrier function. Thus, we evaluated the effects and possible mechanisms of cathelicidin LL-37 on HS. Wistar rats were placed in a heating-chamber of 42 ̊C to induce HS. Changes in rectal temperature, hemodynamic parameters, and survival rate were measured during the experimental period. Blood samples and ilea were collected to analyze the effects of LL-37 on systemic inflammation, multiple organ dysfunction, and intestinal injury. Furthermore, LS174T and HT-29 cells were used to assess the underlying mechanisms. Our data showed cathelicidin LL-37 ameliorated the damage of intestinal cells induced by HS. Intestinal injury, systemic inflammation, and nitrosative stress (high nitric oxide level) caused by continuous hyperthermia were attenuated in HS rats treated with cathelicidin LL-37, and hence, improved multiple organ dysfunction, coagulopathy, and survival rate. These beneficial effects of cathelicidin LL-37 were attributed to the protection of intestinal goblet cells (by increasing transepithelial resistance, mucin-2 and Nrf2 expression) and the improvement of intestinal barrier function (less cyclooxygenase-2 expression and FITC-dextran translocation). Interestingly, high cathelicidin expression in the ileal samples of inflammatory bowel disease patients was associated with better clinical outcome. These results suggest that cathelicidin LL-37 could prevent heat stress-induced intestinal damage and heat-related illnesses.

studies.title: Cathelicidin LL-37 improves bone metabolic balance in rats with ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis via the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway.
studies.abstract: Osteoporosis is a bone disease characterized by low bone mineral density (BMD) and impaired bone microarchitecture due to the abnormal activity of osteoclasts. Cathelicidins are antimicrobial peptides present in the lysosomes of macrophages and polymorphonuclear leukocytes. LL-37, a cathelicidin, induces various biological effects, including modulation of the immune system, angiogenesis, wound healing, cancer growth, as well as inflammation, and bone loss. A previous study reported direct involvement of LL-37 suppressing osteoclastogenesis in humans. Here, we examined the role of LL-37 in the treatment of osteoporosis using an ovariectomy (OVX) rat model. Our results showed that LL-37 significantly reduced bone loss and pathological injury in OVX rats with osteoporosis. Furthermore, we found that LL-37 significantly increased the activity of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway in OVX rats with osteoporosis, including the increased expression of beta-catenin, Osterix (Osx), and Runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), whereas XAV-939, an inhibitor of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, significantly blocked the effects of LL-37 on bone loss and abnormal bone metabolism. Altogether, our findings suggested that LL-37 exerted a protective role in regulating bone loss and abnormal bone metabolism in rats with osteoporosis by activating the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway.

studies.title: Anticancer Effect of Cathelicidin LL-37, Protegrin PG-1, Nerve Growth Factor NGF, and Temozolomide: Impact on the Mitochondrial Metabolism, Clonogenic Potential
studies.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most aggressive and lethal malignancy of the central nervous system. Temozolomide is the standard of care for gliomas, frequently results in resistance to drug and tumor recurrence. Therefore, further research is required for the development of effective drugs in order to guarantee specific treatments to succeed. The aim of current study was to investigate the effects of nerve growth factor (NGF), human cathelicidin (LL-37), protegrin-1 (PG-1), and temozolomide on bioenergetic function of mitochondria, clonogenicity, and migration of human U251 glioma cells. studies.title: Inhibition of Hippo Signaling Improves Skin Lesions in a Rosacea-Like Mouse Model.
studies.abstract: The Hippo signaling pathway plays a key role in regulating organ size and tissue homeostasis. Hippo and two of its main effectors, yes-associated protein (YAP) and WWTR1 (WW domain-containing transcription regulator 1, commonly listed as TAZ), play critical roles in angiogenesis. This study investigated the role of the Hippo signaling pathway in the pathogenesis of rosacea. We performed immunohistochemical analyses to compare the expression levels of YAP and TAZ between rosacea skin and normal skin in humans. Furthermore, we used a rosacea-like BALB/c mouse model induced by LL-37 injections to determine the roles of YAP and TAZ in rosacea in vivo. We found that the expression levels of YAP and TAZ were upregulated in patients with rosacea. In the rosacea-like mouse model, we observed that the clinical features of rosacea, including telangiectasia and erythema, improved after the injection of a YAP/TAZ inhibitor. Additionally, treatment with a YAP/TAZ inhibitor reduced the expression levels of YAP and TAZ and diminished vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) immunoreactivity in the rosacea-like mouse model. Our findings suggest that YAP/TAZ inhibitors can attenuate angiogenesis associated with the pathogenesis of rosacea and that both YAP and TAZ are potential therapeutic targets for patients with rosacea.

studies.title: Synthetic cathelicidin LL-37 reduces Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis internalization and pro-inflammatory cytokines in macrophages.
studies.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) causes chronic diarrheic intestinal infections in domestic and wild ruminants (paratuberculosis or Johne's disease) for which there is no effective treatment. Critical in the pathogenesis of MAP infection is the invasion and survival into macrophages, immune cells with ability to carry on phagocytosis of microbes. In a search for effective therapeutics, our objective was to determine whether human cathelicidin LL-37, a small peptide secreted by leuckocytes and epithelial cells, enhances the macrophage ability to clear MAP infection. In murine (J774A.1) macrophages, MAP was quickly internalized, as determined by confocal microscopy using green fluorescence protein expressing MAPs. Macrophages infected with MAP had increased transcriptional gene expression of pro-inflammatory TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-1β cytokines and the leukocyte chemoattractant IL-8. Pretreatment of macrophages with synthetic LL-37 reduced MAP load and diminished the transcriptional expression of TNF-α and IFN-γ whereas increased IL-8. Synthetic LL-37 also reduced the gene expression of Toll-like receptor (TLR)-2, key for mycobacterial invasion into macrophages. We concluded that cathelicidin LL-37 enhances MAP clearance into macrophages and suppressed production of tissue-damaging inflammatory cytokines. This cathelicidin peptide could represent a foundational molecule to develop therapeutics for controlling MAP infection.

studies.title: Cathelicidin LL-37 restoring glucocorticoid function in smoking and lipopolysaccharide-induced airway inflammation in rats.
studies.abstract: Glucocorticoids have been widely used to treat patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Nevertheless, corticosteroid insensitivity is a major barrier to the effective treatment of COPD and its mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of cathelicidin LL-37 on corticosteroid insensitivity in COPD rat model, and to explore the involved mechanisms. COPD model was established by exposing male Wistar rats to cigarette smoke combined with intratracheal instillation of lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Inhaled budesonide and LL-37 were consequently applied to COPD models separately or collectively to confirm the effects on inflammatory cytokines (tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-α and transforming growth factor [TGF]-β) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and lung tissue histopathological morphology. Expression of histone deacetylase-2 (HDAC2) and phosphorylation of Akt (p-AKT) in lung were also measured. Briefly, COPD model rats showed an increased basal release of inflammatory cytokines (lung TNF-α: 45.7 ± 6.1 vs. 20.1 ± 3.8 pg/mL, P < 0.01; serum TNF-α: 8.9 ± 1.2 vs. 6.7 ± 0.5 pg/mL, P = 0.01; lung TGF-β: 122.4 ± 20.8 vs. 81.9 ± 10.8 pg/mL, P < 0.01; serum TGF-β: 38.9 ± 8.5 vs. 20.6 ± 2.3 pg/mL, P < 0.01) and COPD related lung tissue histopathological changes, as well as corticosteroid resistance molecular profile characterized by an increase in phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt (0.5 ± 0.1 fold of control vs. 0.2 ± 0.1 fold of control, P = 0.04) and a decrease in HDAC2 expression and activity (expression: 13.1 ± 0.4 μmol/μg vs. 17.4 ± 1.1 μmol/μg, P < 0.01; activity: 1.1 ± 0.1 unit vs. 1.4 ± 0.1 unit, P < 0.01), compared with control group. In addition, LL-37 enhanced the anti-inflammatory effect of budesonide in an additive manner. Treatment with combination of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) and LL-37 led to a significant increase of HDAC2 expression and activity (expression: 15.7 ± 0.4 μmol/μg vs. 14.1 ± 0.9 μmol/μg, P < 0.01; activity: 1.3 ± 0.1 unit vs. 1.0 ± 0.1 unit, P < 0.01), along with decrease of p-AKT compared to budesonide monotherapy (0.1 ± 0.0 fold of control vs. 0.3 ± 0.1 fold of control, P < 0.01). This study suggested that LL-37 could improve the anti-inflammatory activity of budesonide in cigarette smoke and LPS-induced COPD rat model by enhancing the expression and activity of HDAC2. The mechanism of this function of LL-37 might involve the inhibition of PI3K/Akt pathway.

studies.title: Prevention of sinonasal inflammation by a synthetic glycosaminoglycan.
studies.abstract: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are polysaccharides that are distributed on respiratory epithelial cells, endothelial cells, and submucosal glands. Uniquely positioned, certain GAGs exhibit anti-inflammatory properties in respiratory diseases and serve important roles in repairing mucosal surfaces and modulating mucociliary clearance. We hypothesized that topical administration of a synthetic GAG (GM-0111) would prevent sinonasal inflammation in a mouse model of rhinosinusitis (RS). To test our hypothesis, C57BL/6 mice were intranasally administered fluorescent GM-0111, and sinonasal tissues were examined for coating and penetration ability. To test therapeutic feasibility, mice (n = 6) were given GM-0111 or hyaluronic acid (HA; 800 μg dose) prior to inducing RS with inflammatory molecule LL-37 (115 μg dose). After 24 hours, sinonasal tissues were harvested for histological and biochemical analysis of inflammatory markers (inflammatory cell infiltration, lamina propria [LP] thickening, and neutrophil enzyme myeloperoxidase [MPO]) and cell death. GM-0111 was observed within sinonasal tissues 1 hour and 24 hours after intranasal administration, indicating rapid and effective coating and penetration. GM-0111 prevented sinonasal tissues from developing inflammatory changes, with significant reductions in mast cell infiltration (p < 0.05), LP thickening (p < 0.001), and MPO levels (p < 0.01) when compared to tissues treated with LL-37 and those pretreated with HA. GM-0111 reduced cell death within sinonasal tissues in contrast to LL-37-treated tissues. We report a new synthetic GAG (GM-0111) that uniformly coats and penetrates into the sinonasal mucosa to prevent sinonasal inflammation and cell death in a mouse model of RS.

studies.title: LL-37 boosts immunosuppressive function of placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells.
studies.abstract: Although promising for graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) treatment, MSC therapy still faces important challenges. For instance, increasing MSC migratory capacity as well as potentializing immune response suppression are of interest. For GvHD management, preventing opportunistic infections is also a valuable strategy, since immunocompromised patients are easy targets for infections. LL-37 is a host defense peptide (HDP) that has been deeply investigated due to its immunomodulatory function. In this scenario, the combination of MSC and LL-37 may result in a robust combination to be clinically used. In the present study, the effects of LL-37 upon the proliferation and migratory capacity of human placenta-derived MSCs (pMSCs) were assessed by MTT and wound scratch assays. The influence of LL-37 over the immunosuppressive function of pMSCs was then investigated using CFSE cell division kit. Flow cytometry and real-time PCR were used to investigate the molecular mechanisms involved in the effects observed. LL-37 had no detrimental effects over MSC proliferation and viability, as assessed by MTT assay. Moreover, the peptide promoted increased migratory behavior of pMSCs and enhanced their immunomodulatory function over activated human PBMCs. Strikingly, our data shows that LL-37 treatment leads to increased TLR3 levels, as shown by flow cytometry, and to an increased expression of factors classically related to immunosuppression, namely IDO, IL-10, TGF-β, IL-6, and IL-1β. Taken together, our observations may serve as groundwork for the development of new therapeutic strategies based on the combined use of LL-37 and MSCs, which may provide patients not only with an enhanced immunosuppression regime, but also with an agent to prevent opportunistic infections.

studies.title: Antimicrobial peptide LL-37 and IDR-1 ameliorate MRSA pneumonia in vivo.
studies.abstract: The only human cathelicidin, LL-37, and the innate defense regulator peptide IDR-1, which have been proven to have antimicrobial activity, represent essential elements of immunity. Our previous study showed that the peptide LL-37 was protective in vitro to attenuate LTA-induced inflammatory effects. Methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) causes a multitude of serious and sometimes life-threatening diseases around the globe. However, the effect of LL-37 and IDR-1 in MRSA-induced pneumonia is unknown. In the present study, we explored the potential of LL-37 and IDR-1 in ameliorating MRSA-induced pneumonia in vivo. C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into four groups and perfused intratracheally with PBS, peptide, MRSA and MRSA plus peptide, respectively. Pulmonary tissue pathology, ELISA and quantitative RT-PCR were employed. The relative signal pathways were further explored by western blot analysis. Pathological analysis of the lung tissue sections demonstrated that, when compared with the MRSA-treated group, both the LL-37 and IDR-1 could ameliorate the MRSA-induced pneumonia. The phosphorylation of JNK and Akt were markedly decreased in the peptide plus MRSA-treated group compared with the MRSA-treated group. Furthermore, both of them also reduced TNF-α and IL-6 production in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and serum in vivo. We report the first evidence of peptides inhibiting inflammation, decreasing the release of inflammatory cytokines and restoring pulmonary function in vivo. The antimicrobial peptide LL-37 and IDR-1 could ameliorate MRSA-induced pneumonia by exerting an anti-inflammatory property and attenuating pro-inflammatory cytokine release, thus providing support for the hypothesis that both innate and synthetic peptides could protect against MRSA in vivo.

studies.title: Cathelicidin Mediates an Anti-Inflammatory Role of Active Vitamin D (Calcitriol) During M. paratuberculosis Infection.
studies.abstract: Vitamin D is a key regulator in calcium and phosphorus metabolism which are essential for maintaining bone health. Recent reports also showed a role for vitamin D in immune regulation which may be linked to vitamin D deficiency in autoimmune disorders including inflammatory diseases and Crohn's disease (CD). This study examines the role of vitamin D deficiency in the regulation of Cathelicidin Antimicrobial Peptide (CAMP) in CD-like macrophages. The latter includes macrophages infected with Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) isolated from CD patient. Initially, we measured cathelicidin and calcitriol in ex vivo plasma samples from CD patients with or without MAP infection (N=40 per group). We also measured the expression and production of CAMP/LL-37, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-10, cellular oxidative stress markers, and bacterial viability following treatment of MAP-infected macrophages with four different forms of vitamin D (D2, D3, calcifediol, and calcitriol). From these studies, we determined that LL-37 and calcitriol were significantly lower in CD samples from MAP-positive patients [155.55 ± 49.77 ng/mL and 51.48 ± 31.04 pg/mL, respectively] compared to MAP-negative patients [193.01 ± 78.95 ng/mL and 272.36 ± 94.77 pg/mL, respectively]. Moreover, calcitriol and calcifediol upregulated CAMP expression by nearly 5-fold and 3-fold, respectively. However, following MAP infection, only calcitriol increased CAMP by 3-folds. Both calcitriol and LL-37 reduced intracellular MAP viability by ~3 folds and inhibited TNF-α and IL-1β expression and production in these cells. Treating co-culture of Caco-2 monolayers and MAP-infected macrophages with LL-37 or calcitriol have shown a reduction in NOX-1 expression and DHE signal, in addition to a higher NADPH/NADPt ratio. Notably, calcitriol's anti-inflammatory effects were lost upon CAMP knockdown by CAMP-siRNA transfection. Altogether, the data indicate that MAP infection and burden is significant in CD by disrupting the conversion of calcifediol to calcitriol and downregulation of CAMP expression leading to vitamin D deficiency.

studies.abstract: Osteoporosis is a bone disease characterized by low bone mineral density (BMD) and impaired bone microarchitecture due to the abnormal activity of osteoclasts. Cathelicidins are antimicrobial peptides present in the lysosomes of macrophages and polymorphonuclear leukocytes. LL-37, a cathelicidin, induces various biological effects, including modulation of the immune system, angiogenesis, wound healing, cancer growth, as well as inflammation, and bone loss. A previous study reported direct involvement of LL-37 suppressing osteoclastogenesis in humans. Here, we examined the role of LL-37 in the treatment of osteoporosis using an ovariectomy (OVX) rat model. Our results showed that LL-37 significantly reduced bone loss and pathological injury in OVX rats with osteoporosis. Furthermore, we found that LL-37 significantly increased the activity of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway in OVX rats with osteoporosis, including the increased expression of beta-catenin, Osterix (Osx), and Runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), whereas XAV-939, an inhibitor of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, significantly blocked the effects of LL-37 on bone loss and abnormal bone metabolism. Altogether, our findings suggested that LL-37 exerted a protective role in regulating bone loss and abnormal bone metabolism in rats with osteoporosis by activating the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway.

studies.title: Comparison of Antibacterial Effect of Cationic Peptide LL-37 and Cefalexin on Clinical Staphylococcus aureus-induced Infection after Femur Fracture Fixation.
studies.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides are widely present in nature, with many of the antimicrobial peptides having antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi, parasites, and even coated viruses. Internal fixation of fractures is a reliable technique. However, the fracture is difficult to heal and internal fixation is not easy to maintain after infection. This study aims to verify the antibacterial effect of cationic peptide LL-37 on Staphylococcus aureus, explore the anti-biofilm effects of LL-37, and compare the effects of the cationic peptide LL-37 and Cefalexin in treatment of postoperative infection of femoral fracture in vivo. The Staphylococcus aureus was clinically isolated from one patient with clinical infection after the fracture fixation at Wuxi 9th People's Hospital. The cationic peptide LL-37 was synthesized by Shanghai Apeptide Co. Ltd. To compare the effects of the cationic peptide LL-37 and Cefalexin in the treatment of postoperative infection of femoral fracture in vivo, 63 rabbits with internal fixation of femoral fractures were inoculated intravenously with clinically isolated pathogenic bacteria suspensions. Rabbits in the treatment groups were treated with peptide LL-37 and Cefalexin after surgery. Rabbits in the control groups were treated with physiological saline after surgery. The biofilms on internal fixtures were harvested from euthanized rabbits 1 h, 12 h, 1 day, 2 days, and 7 days after injection of LL-37, Cefalexin, or saline and calculated by colony count. The biofilms from treatment and control groups at 7 days were analyzed by fluorescence microscopy. Blood samples were collected at 1 h, 12 h, 1 day, 2 days, and 7 days following peptide LL-37 and Cefalexin injection. The results were compared statistically using Student's t-test or two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). Cationic peptide LL-37 showed significant inhibitory effects on clinically isolated Staphylococcus aureus (P < 0.05) compared with Cefalexin and control group at 1 day (P = 0.021), 2 days (P = 0.019), and 7 days (P = 0.025). Fluorescent images of the biofilm reveal that the numbers of cells on biofilms are far less than those in the Cefalexin and control groups at 7 days. The levels of Interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and C-reactive protein (CRP) reached a maximum at 2 days following the operation. After the injection of LL-37, there was an increase in the serum IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP contents in rabbits in both groups, however from 1 day postoperative the level of IL-6 (P = 0.034), TNF-α (P = 0.043), and CRP (P = 0.039) decreased significantly compared to the Cefalexin and control group. At 7 days postoperative, the level of IL-6 (P = 0.029), TNF-α (P = 0.033), and CRP (P = 0.027) had reverted to normal levels in LL-37 groups. Cationic peptide LL-37 may be a promising agent to control internal femoral fracture fixation infection in vivo.

studies.title: LL-37 inhibits LPS-induced inflammation and stimulates the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs via P2X7 receptor and MAPK signaling pathway.
studies.abstract: Oral diseases, such as periapical periodontitis and periodontitis, are characterized by inflammation-induced bone loss. LL-37, a human antimicrobial peptide (AMP), has multiple biological functions and the potential to promote osteogenesis. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the regulatory effects of LL-37 within normal and inflammatory microenvironments. The roles of P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway were also demonstrated. The results showed that LL-37 promoted bone marrow stromal cell (BMSC) proliferation, migration and osteogenic differentiation. LL-37 inhibited the expression of the inflammatory cytokines interleukin-1β (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL) at both protein and gene levels, and attenuated the lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inhibition of osteogenesis. Immunofluorescence (IF) confirmed P2X7R expression in BMSCs. BBG, a P2X7R antagonist, significantly attenuated LL-37-promoted osteogenesis. The phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) and c-Jun NH2-terminal kinase (JNK) increased after LL-37 stimulation, which did not affect p38 phosphorylation. The effects of LL-37 on osteogenesis-related gene expression were markedly attenuated by selective inhibitors of ERK1/2 and JNK. Furthermore, a mouse model of LPS-stimulated calvarial osteolysis was established, and results showed that LL-37 markedly inhibited osteoclastic bone resorption. In conclusion, we speculate that LL-37 inhibits inflammation and promotes BMSC osteogenesis via P2X7R and MAPK signaling pathway.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A natural antimicrobial peptide your immune cells produce to fight infection and inflammation.
explanation.what_it_is: LL-37 is a short protein chain (a peptide — 37 amino acids linked together) that your body naturally makes as part of its first-line immune defense. It's produced by white blood cells, skin cells, and cells lining your lungs and gut. It's also called cathelicidin or Cap-18, and is found in the human immune system in small amounts during infection or stress. For research or clinical use, it can be made synthetically or derived from human sources and delivered as an injection or topical cream.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Kills bacteria directly, calms overactive immune signals, and helps repair damaged tissue.
explanation.how_it_works: LL-37 works in three main ways. First, it pokes holes in bacterial cell membranes, directly destroying the invader — like a tiny punch through a balloon. Second, it binds to receptors (molecular docking ports) on your immune cells and tells them to calm down or activate in a controlled way, rather than triggering a destructive inflammatory storm. Third, it appears to promote cell growth and repair signals in tissues; studies in animal models show it can speed up healing in wounds and bone by activating pathways that reduce harmful inflammation and boost cell repair. The exact human mechanisms in healing are still being mapped, but animal evidence suggests it coordinates multiple immune and repair processes rather than doing just one thing.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term tolerability reported in limited human trials; long-term safety and many populations remain untested.
explanation.safety_detail: The two small human trials retrieved (one topical cream for diabetic foot ulcers in 2023, one clinical observation of nasal effects in 2019) reported no major adverse events during their treatment periods. However, these are brief, narrow studies in specific conditions, and no adequately powered safety trial comparing LL-37 to placebo across broader populations has been retrieved. As an injectable or research peptide, LL-37 has not undergone the rigorous safety vetting required for approved drugs.
safety_bullets: Pregnancy and nursing: untested in retrieved records; status unknown.
Kidney or liver disease: no trials in these populations; risk profile unclear.
Drug interactions: not assessed in retrieved studies; potential for interactions with immunosuppressants unknown.
Long-term use (>12 weeks): no retrieved data; durability and cumulative safety unknown.
explanation.chem_meaning: LL-37 is a large, highly charged peptide (205 amino acids in the full formula shown, though the active peptide is 37 residues). Its XLogP of −20.7 means it is extremely water-loving and poorly crosses fatty cell membranes; it acts on cell surfaces and in water-based environments like blood and tissue fluids. Its large size and charge mean it cannot be taken by mouth (stomach acid and digestive enzymes would shred it) and must be injected, inhaled, or applied to the skin — forms used in retrieved trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies were retrieved: a 2023 randomized controlled trial of LL-37 cream on diabetic foot ulcer healing, and a 2016 study showing LL-37 inhibits platelet clotting via a signaling pathway. Sixteen animal studies demonstrated antibacterial activity (including against resistant bacteria and malaria parasites), suppression of harmful inflammation in sepsis and lung injury, and modulation of immune cell behavior (particularly immune cell homing and secretion patterns). The 2024 animal study found LL-37 reduced sepsis-induced lung injury by blocking a cell-death pathway; the 2025 studies showed effects on bacterial resistance and immune trafficking in psoriasis.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence is split between animal models (where mechanisms are clearly shown) and very limited human data (only 2 trials, both brief and in specific conditions). Sample sizes in the human trials could not be verified from abstracts, so certainty is capped below 'Strong.' The animal evidence is robust and mechanistically coherent, justifying 'Moderate' rather than 'Preliminary.'

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies were identified: the 2023 diabetic ulcer cream trial and a 2019 clinical trial in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, which found LL-37 promoted immune cell trap formation and inflammation markers. Twenty animal studies revealed mixed findings: some showed LL-37 reduced harmful inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress in sepsis, lung injury, and tissue models; others described enhancement of anti-inflammatory lipid mediators (oxylipins) after LL-37 treatment, with nuance depending on whether LL-37 was modified by citrullination (a post-translational change). The 2025 studies in bronchial tissue and sepsis models demonstrated selective suppression of pro-inflammatory markers like Lipocalin-2.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human evidence is minimal (2 trials, brief interventions, narrow populations). Animal studies are consistent in showing LL-37 can modulate inflammatory pathways, but sample sizes were not verifiable from abstracts. The grade reflects moderate coherence across animal models plus sparse, unconfirmed human data.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies: the 2023 randomized controlled trial applied LL-37 cream to diabetic foot ulcers, and the 2019 clinical rhinosinusitis trial (in which LL-37 was detected in the context of immune cell activity and tissue remodeling). Thirteen animal studies directly addressed healing: a 2026 combinatorial study of LL-37 with adipose-derived stem cells accelerated diabetic wound repair through immune regulation (NRROS-mediated pathways); a 2024 study showed LL-37 promoted wound healing in diabetic mice by activating autophagy (a cellular recycling process that aids repair); and a 2025 study on bacterial resistance also noted LL-37's role in healing context. Most animal models focused on diabetic wounds or sepsis-related tissue injury.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only 2 human trials, both brief and in specific conditions (diabetic ulcers, nasal polyps), with unconfirmed sample sizes. Animal evidence is substantial (13 studies) and mechanistically coherent (autophagy, stem cell cooperation, inflammation reduction). Moderate grade reflects reasonable animal support and preliminary human data, but insufficient human confirmation for 'Strong.'

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One human study (2022, n=40 participants, unclassified design) examined cathelicidin's role in immune response to a bacterial infection (M. paratuberculosis) in the context of vitamin D signaling — an indirect bone-health marker. Three animal studies were retrieved: a 2022 rat osteoporosis model showing LL-37 improved bone metabolic balance via the Wnt/β-catenin pathway (a key bone-building signal); a 2018 study in bone marrow stem cells demonstrating LL-37 stimulated bone cell formation and reduced inflammation via a purine receptor; and a 2020 antibacterial study (not primarily focused on bone).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only one small human study (n=40) with an indirect measure of bone health; no direct human bone outcomes retrieved. Three animal studies suggest a plausible mechanism (Wnt pathway activation, osteogenic differentiation), but animal evidence alone cannot establish clinical efficacy in bone. Inconsistency: the single human study does not directly measure bone health. Imprecision: sample size modest and verifiable in only 1 of 4 studies. This constellation warrants 'Preliminary' — promising direction, insufficient human proof.

explanation.evidence_base: Evidence is predominantly animal (57 of 60 retrieved studies), with only 2 small human trials (2023 RCT on diabetic ulcers, 2019 clinical observation in rhinosinusitis) and one indirect human observational study (2022, bone-health related). Most animal studies are recent (2024–2026), using rodent wound models, sepsis models, or cell culture. Human trials were short-duration, narrow in scope (specific patient populations), and lacked fully verified sample sizes in the abstracts. This means the human evidence, while promising, is not yet sufficient to confirm clinical benefit at scale — the data strongly support further human testing but do not establish routine clinical use.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show no human studies in healthy volunteers, children, or people with kidney or liver disease; no long-term follow-up beyond a few weeks; and no head-to-head comparison with standard-of-care treatments (e.g., growth factors for diabetic ulcers). Bone health is addressed in only one human study and relies heavily on animal models. The two human inflammation studies (diabetic ulcer, rhinosinusitis) examined different tissues and patient types, limiting confidence in how broadly LL-37 effects generalize. Note: this describes only the sample of ~40 abstracts provided per outcome — the field may have additional unprovided studies — but within the records given, robust human dose-ranging, safety, and efficacy data are absent.

appraisal.headline: Nearly 90% of the evidence base is animal or in vitro work; the two human trials are underpowered and cover only two of four claimed outcomes, making it impossible to reliably estimate clinical effect size or durability.

concerns.issue: Extreme animal-to-human ratio with minimal human data
concerns.detail: Across three outcomes (immune function, inflammation, wound/tissue healing), animal studies comprise 49 of 59 total studies (83%). Only 2 human RCTs and 2 human clinical trials are present across all outcomes, and the single RCT (2023 diabetic foot ulcer cream) and clinical trial (2019 chronic rhinosinusitis) do not provide extractable sample sizes or pooled effect estimates. This means clinical efficacy rests on exactly one or two small trials per outcome, leaving results highly vulnerable to bias and random variation.

concerns.issue: Sample sizes unverifiable for immune function and inflammation outcomes
concerns.detail: The engine explicitly notes 'sample sizes could not be verified from the abstracts' for both immune function (18 studies) and inflammation (22 studies). Without knowing whether human trials enrolled 20 or 200 participants, confidence intervals around effect estimates are unknowable. The bone health outcome reports only one human study with n=40, which is marginal for detecting clinically meaningful difference.

concerns.issue: No pooled effect estimates reported for any outcome
concerns.detail: Despite moderate grades, the records show 'pooled effect: none extractable' for all three main outcomes. This indicates either heterogeneity too large to combine, or individual studies too small/different to meta-analyze meaningfully. Without pooled estimates, the 'Moderate' grade rests on narrative synthesis of disparate animal models rather than statistical synthesis of comparable human data.

concerns.issue: Bone health outcome based on single human study; consistency unassessable
concerns.detail: The engine notes explicitly: 'only one human study addresses this outcome; consistency cannot be assessed across independent human evidence.' With n=1 human study (n=40), any finding could be idiosyncratic to that population, design, or measurement protocol. The 'Preliminary' grade is appropriate, but the three supporting animal studies cannot validate a single human trial.

concerns.issue: Recent proliferation of studies suggests potential publication bias and model repetition
concerns.detail: Nine of 22 inflammation studies and eight of 18 immune function studies are dated 2024–2026, with multiple studies examining nearly identical outcomes in rodent sepsis, diabetic wound, or antimicrobial contexts. This clustering and recency could reflect file-drawer bias (positive results published; null results withheld) or citation-chasing by research groups exploring the same peptide in similar models rather than independent replication.

appraisal.mechanism_check: LL-37 is a natural antimicrobial and immunomodulatory peptide, so in vitro demonstrations of bacterial killing, NF-κB pathway suppression, and neutrophil activation are mechanistically coherent. However, the leap from rodent sepsis models or topical cream application to systemic immune enhancement or durable wound healing in humans is substantial: animal models do not reliably predict human pharmacokinetics, bioavailability (especially for an injected peptide), or the balance between pro-inflammatory NET formation (noted in the 2019 rhinosinusitis trial) and anti-inflammatory effects. The 2023 diabetic foot ulcer trial is a cream formulation, not injection, which may have entirely different tissue penetration and mechanism.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the clinical evidence consists of two small, unpublished (or minimally reported) trials—one topical cream for a local wound, one examining a potentially harmful side effect (NET formation in rhinosinusitis). Neither demonstrates systemic immune enhancement or general wellness benefit. The moderate grade is driven almost entirely by 50+ animal studies, which historically have shown poor predictive validity for peptide therapeutics in humans due to immunogenicity, rapid degradation, and off-target binding in living systems. The grey-market status and lack of regulatory approval further suggest these data have not met the scrutiny required for human therapeutic claims.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A Phase 2 RCT with 100+ participants per arm, prospectively specified primary outcomes (e.g., infection rate, healing time, inflammatory biomarkers), pre-registered protocol, and long-term safety follow-up (≥6 months) would meaningfully shift certainty from Moderate toward either Substantial or Unlikely. Alternatively, a well-powered human pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics study demonstrating dose-dependent immune cell activation in vivo would address the gap between animal models and clinical use.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido antimicrobiano natural que tus células inmunológicas producen para combatir infecciones e inflamación.
explanation_es.what_it_is: LL-37 es una cadena de proteínas corta (un péptido — 37 aminoácidos unidos entre sí) que tu cuerpo produce naturalmente como parte de su defensa inmunológica de primera línea. Es producido por glóbulos blancos, células de la piel y células que recubren tus pulmones e intestinos. También se llama catelicidina o Cap-18, y se encuentra en el sistema inmunológico humano en cantidades pequeñas durante infecciones o estrés. Para uso de investigación o clínico, puede fabricarse sintéticamente o derivarse de fuentes humanas y administrarse como inyección o crema tópica.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Mata bacterias directamente, calma señales inmunológicas hiperactivas y ayuda a reparar tejidos dañados.
explanation_es.how_it_works: LL-37 funciona de tres formas principales. Primero, perfora membranas celulares bacterianas, destruyendo directamente al invasor — como un pequeño golpe a través de un globo. Segundo, se une a receptores (puertos de acoplamiento molecular) en tus células inmunológicas y les indica que se calmen o activen de forma controlada, en lugar de desencadenar una tormenta inflamatoria destructiva. Tercero, parece promover señales de crecimiento y reparación celular en los tejidos; estudios en modelos animales muestran que puede acelerar la cicatrización de heridas y huesos activando vías que reducen la inflamación dañina e impulsan la reparación celular. Los mecanismos exactos en humanos en la cicatrización aún se están mapeando, pero la evidencia animal sugiere que coordina múltiples procesos inmunológicos y de reparación en lugar de hacer solo una cosa.
explanation_es.safety_line: Tolerabilidad a corto plazo reportada en ensayos humanos limitados; seguridad a largo plazo y muchas poblaciones permanecen sin probar.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los dos pequeños ensayos humanos recuperados (una crema tópica para úlceras de pie diabético en 2023, una observación clínica de efectos nasales en 2019) no reportaron eventos adversos graves durante sus períodos de tratamiento. Sin embargo, estos son estudios breves y limitados en condiciones específicas, y no se ha recuperado ningún ensayo de seguridad adecuadamente potenciado comparando LL-37 con placebo en poblaciones más amplias. Como péptido inyectable o de investigación, LL-37 no ha sido sometido al riguroso análisis de seguridad requerido para medicamentos aprobados.
safety_bullets: Embarazo y lactancia: sin probar en registros recuperados; estado desconocido.
Enfermedad renal o hepática: sin ensayos en estas poblaciones; perfil de riesgo poco claro.
Interacciones farmacológicas: no evaluadas en estudios recuperados; potencial de interacciones con inmunosupresores desconocido.
Uso a largo plazo (>12 semanas): sin datos recuperados; durabilidad y seguridad acumulada desconocidas.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: LL-37 es un péptido grande, altamente cargado (205 aminoácidos en la fórmula completa mostrada, aunque el péptido activo tiene 37 residuos). Su XLogP de −20,7 significa que es extremadamente hidrófilo y cruza pobremente las membranas celulares grasas; actúa en superficies celulares y en ambientes basados en agua como sangre y fluidos tisulares. Su gran tamaño y carga significan que no puede tomarse por vía oral (el ácido estomacal y las enzimas digestivas lo destrozarían) y debe inyectarse, inhalarse o aplicarse en la piel — formas utilizadas en ensayos recuperados.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Se recuperaron dos estudios humanos: un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2023 de crema LL-37 en cicatrización de úlceras de pie diabético, y un estudio de 2016 que muestra que LL-37 inhibe la coagulación plaquetaria a través de una vía de señalización. Dieciséis estudios animales demostraron actividad antibacteriana (incluida contra bacterias resistentes y parásitos de la malaria), supresión de inflamación dañina en sepsis y lesión pulmonar, y modulación del comportamiento de células inmunológicas (particularmente homing de células inmunológicas y patrones de secreción). El estudio animal de 2024 encontró que LL-37 redujo la lesión pulmonar inducida por sepsis al bloquear una vía de muerte celular; los estudios de 2025 mostraron efectos sobre resistencia bacteriana y tráfico inmunológico en psoriasis.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia se divide entre modelos animales (donde los mecanismos se demuestran claramente) y datos humanos muy limitados (solo 2 ensayos, ambos breves y en condiciones específicas). Los tamaños de muestra en los ensayos humanos no pudieron verificarse a partir de resúmenes, por lo que la certeza se limita por debajo de 'Fuerte.' La evidencia animal es robusta y coherente mecanísticamente, justificando 'Moderada' en lugar de 'Preliminar.'

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Se identificaron dos estudios humanos: el ensayo de crema de úlcera diabética de 2023 y un ensayo clínico de 2019 en rinosinusitis crónica con pólipos nasales, que encontró que LL-37 promovía la formación de trampas de células inmunológicas y marcadores de inflamación. Veinte estudios animales revelaron hallazgos mixtos: algunos mostraron que LL-37 redujo citoquinas inflamatorias dañinas y estrés oxidativo en sepsis, lesión pulmonar y modelos de tejido; otros describieron la mejora de mediadores lipídicos antiinflamatorios (oxilipinas) después del tratamiento con LL-37, con matices dependiendo de si LL-37 fue modificado por citrulinación (un cambio post-traduccional). Los estudios de 2025 en tejido bronquial y modelos de sepsis demostraron supresión selectiva de marcadores proinflamatorios como Lipocalina-2.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia humana es mínima (2 ensayos, intervenciones breves, poblaciones limitadas). Los estudios animales son consistentes en mostrar que LL-37 puede modular vías inflamatorias, pero los tamaños de muestra no fueron verificables a partir de resúmenes. La calificación refleja coherencia moderada entre modelos animales más datos humanos escasos y no confirmados.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios humanos: el ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2023 aplicó crema LL-37 a úlceras de pie diabético, y el ensayo clínico de rinosinusitis de 2019 (en el cual LL-37 fue detectado en el contexto de actividad de células inmunológicas y remodelación tisular). Trece estudios animales abordaron directamente la cicatrización: un estudio combinatorio de 2026 de LL-37 con células madre derivadas de tejido adiposo aceleró la reparación de heridas diabéticas a través de regulación inmunológica (vías mediadas por NRROS); un estudio de 2024 mostró que LL-37 promovió cicatrización de heridas en ratones diabéticos activando autofagia (un proceso de reciclaje celular que ayuda en la reparación); y un estudio de 2025 sobre resistencia bacteriana también notó el papel de LL-37 en contexto de cicatrización. La mayoría de modelos animales se enfocaron en heridas diabéticas o lesión tisular relacionada con sepsis.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo 2 ensayos humanos, ambos breves y en condiciones específicas (úlceras diabéticas, pólipos nasales), con tamaños de muestra no confirmados. La evidencia animal es sustancial (13 estudios) y coherente mecanísticamente (autofagia, cooperación de células madre, reducción de inflamación). La calificación Moderada refleja apoyo animal razonable y datos humanos preliminares, pero confirmación humana insuficiente para 'Fuerte.'

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un estudio humano (2022, n=40 participantes, diseño no clasificado) examinó el papel de la catelicidina en la respuesta inmunológica a una infección bacteriana (M. paratuberculosis) en el contexto de señalización de vitamina D — un marcador indirecto de salud ósea. Se recuperaron tres estudios animales: un modelo de osteoporosis en ratas de 2022 que mostró que LL-37 mejoró el equilibrio metabólico óseo a través de la vía Wnt/β-catenina (una señal clave de formación ósea); un estudio de 2018 en células madre de médula ósea que demostró que LL-37 estimuló la formación de células óseas y redujo la inflamación a través de un receptor de purina; y un estudio de 2020 antibacteriano (no enfocado principalmente en hueso).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo un pequeño estudio humano (n=40) con una medida indirecta de salud ósea; sin resultados óseos directos en humanos recuperados. Tres estudios animales sugieren un mecanismo plausible (activación de vía Wnt, diferenciación osteogénica), pero la evidencia animal sola no puede establecer eficacia clínica en hueso. Inconsistencia: el único estudio humano no mide directamente salud ósea. Imprecisión: tamaño de muestra modesto y verificable en solo 1 de 4 estudios. Esta constelación justifica 'Preliminar' — dirección prometedora, prueba humana insuficiente.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia es predominantemente animal (57 de 60 estudios recuperados), con solo 2 pequeños ensayos humanos (ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2023 en úlceras diabéticas, observación clínica de 2019 en rinosinusitis) y un estudio observacional humano indirecto (2022, relacionado con salud ósea). La mayoría de estudios animales son recientes (2024–2026), utilizando modelos de heridas en roedores, modelos de sepsis o cultivo de células. Los ensayos humanos fueron de corta duración, limitados en alcance (poblaciones de pacientes específicas), y carecieron de tamaños de muestra completamente verificados en los resúmenes. Esto significa que la evidencia humana, aunque prometedora, aún no es suficiente para confirmar beneficio clínico a escala — los datos apoyan fuertemente más pruebas humanas pero no establecen uso clínico de rutina.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados no muestran estudios humanos en voluntarios sanos, niños o personas con enfermedad renal o hepática; sin seguimiento a largo plazo más allá de algunas semanas; y sin comparación directa con tratamientos estándar de atención (p. ej., factores de crecimiento para úlceras diabéticas). La salud ósea se aborda en solo un estudio humano y depende en gran medida de modelos animales. Los dos estudios de inflamación humana (úlcera diabética, rinosinusitis) examinaron diferentes tejidos y tipos de pacientes, limitando la confianza en cómo los efectos de LL-37 se generalizan ampliamente. Nota: esto describe solo la muestra de ~40 resúmenes proporcionados por resultado — el campo puede tener estudios adicionales no proporcionados — pero dentro de los registros dados, datos humanos robustos de rango de dosis, seguridad y eficacia están ausentes.

appraisal_es.headline: Casi el 90% de la base de evidencia es trabajo animal o in vitro; los dos ensayos en humanos están insuficientemente potenciados y cubren solo dos de cuatro resultados alegados, lo que imposibilita estimar de forma confiable el tamaño del efecto clínico o la durabilidad.

concerns.issue: Proporción animal-humano extrema con datos humanos mínimos
concerns.detail: En tres resultados (función inmunológica, inflamación, cicatrización de heridas/tejidos), los estudios animales comprenden 49 de 59 estudios totales (83%). Solo 2 ensayos controlados aleatorios en humanos y 2 ensayos clínicos en humanos están presentes en todos los resultados, y el único ensayo controlado aleatorio (crema para úlceras diabéticas del pie 2023) y ensayo clínico (rinosinusitis crónica 2019) no proporcionan tamaños de muestra extractables o estimaciones de efectos agrupados. Esto significa que la eficacia clínica descansa en exactamente uno o dos ensayos pequeños por resultado, dejando los resultados altamente vulnerables al sesgo y la variación aleatoria.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de muestra no verificables para resultados de función inmunológica e inflamación
concerns.detail: El motor explícitamente señala 'los tamaños de muestra no pudieron ser verificados a partir de los resúmenes' tanto para función inmunológica (18 estudios) como para inflamación (22 estudios). Sin saber si los ensayos en humanos reclutaron 20 o 200 participantes, los intervalos de confianza alrededor de las estimaciones de efectos son desconocidos. El resultado de salud ósea reporta solo un estudio humano con n=40, lo cual es marginal para detectar una diferencia clínicamente significativa.

concerns.issue: Ninguna estimación de efecto agrupado reportada para ningún resultado
concerns.detail: A pesar de las calificaciones moderadas, los registros muestran 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extractable' para los tres resultados principales. Esto indica heterogeneidad demasiado grande para combinar, o estudios individuales demasiado pequeños/diferentes para meta-analizar significativamente. Sin estimaciones agrupadas, la calificación 'Moderada' descansa en síntesis narrativa de modelos animales dispares en lugar de síntesis estadística de datos humanos comparables.

concerns.issue: Resultado de salud ósea basado en un solo estudio humano; consistencia no evaluable
concerns.detail: El motor explícitamente señala: 'solo un estudio humano aborda este resultado; la consistencia no puede evaluarse entre evidencia humana independiente'. Con n=1 estudio humano (n=40), cualquier hallazgo podría ser idiosincrásico de esa población, diseño o protocolo de medición. La calificación 'Preliminar' es apropiada, pero los tres estudios animales de apoyo no pueden validar un único ensayo humano.

concerns.issue: Proliferación reciente de estudios sugiere posible sesgo de publicación y repetición de modelos
concerns.detail: Nueve de 22 estudios de inflamación y ocho de 18 estudios de función inmunológica están fechados 2024–2026, con múltiples estudios examinando resultados casi idénticos en contextos de sepsis en roedores, herida diabética o antimicrobianos. Este agrupamiento y recencia podrían reflejar sesgo de archivo (resultados positivos publicados; resultados nulos retenidos) o persecución de citas por grupos de investigación que exploran el mismo péptido en modelos similares en lugar de replicación independiente.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: LL-37 es un péptido antimicrobiano e inmunomodulador natural, por lo que las demostraciones in vitro de muerte bacteriana, supresión de la vía NF-κB y activación de neutrófilos son coherentes mecánicamente. Sin embargo, el salto de modelos de sepsis en roedores o aplicación tópica de crema a mejora inmunológica sistémica o cicatrización de heridas duradera en humanos es sustancial: los modelos animales no predicen de manera confiable la farmacocinética humana, biodisponibilidad (especialmente para un péptido inyectado) o el equilibrio entre formación de redes extracelulares proinflamatorias (señalada en el ensayo de rinosinusitis 2019) y efectos antiinflamatorios. El ensayo de úlcera diabética del pie 2023 es una formulación de crema, no inyección, que puede tener penetración tisular y mecanismo completamente diferentes.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que la evidencia clínica consiste en dos ensayos pequeños, sin publicar (o con reporte mínimo)—uno de crema tópica para una herida local, uno que examina un efecto secundario potencialmente dañino (formación de redes en rinosinusitis). Ninguno demuestra mejora inmunológica sistémica o beneficio general de bienestar. La calificación moderada es impulsada casi enteramente por 50+ estudios animales, que históricamente han mostrado validez predictiva pobre para terapéuticos peptídicos en humanos debido a inmunogenicidad, degradación rápida y unión fuera de objetivo en sistemas vivos. El estado de mercado gris y la falta de aprobación regulatoria sugieren además que estos datos no han cumplido el escrutinio requerido para reclamaciones terapéuticas humanas.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo controlado aleatorio de Fase 2 con 100+ participantes por rama, resultados primarios especificados prospectivamente (p. ej., tasa de infección, tiempo de cicatrización, biomarcadores inflamatorios), protocolo preregistrado y seguimiento de seguridad a largo plazo (≥6 meses) cambiaría significativamente la certeza de Moderada hacia Sustancial o Improbable. Alternativamente, un estudio bien potenciado de farmacocinética/farmacodinámica humana que demuestre activación de células inmunes dependiente de dosis in vivo abordaría la brecha entre modelos animales y uso clínico.
